rounds.text: Ashok Leyland’s financial health is undermined by a precarious liquidity position, evidenced by a negative operating cash flow of Rs -4,895 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -7,712 Cr in Mar 2026 [E35, E36]. This cash burn is exacerbated by a significant reliance on debt, with borrowings ballooning to Rs 63,936 Cr and a debt-to-equity ratio of 4.49x, indicating that liabilities now substantially exceed net worth [E38, E40]. Valuation metrics appear stretched, as the stock trades at a price-to-book ratio of 7.23x, significantly higher than the sector benchmark of 2.6x [E2, E7]. Furthermore, institutional confidence is waning, as evidenced by negative money flow and a reduction in holdings by domestic institutions [E44, E45, E71]. While the company has shown historical profit growth, recent data highlights decelerating earnings growth and inconsistent operating margins [E32, E33, E70]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong 24.37% ROE compared to the 10.54% sector benchmark and has delivered 84% profit growth over the last five years [E9, E19, E60]. Despite these historical achievements, the combination of extreme leverage, negative cash conversion, and a high valuation relative to book value suggests the current market price may not be supported by the underlying quality of the balance sheet [E2, E34, E38].
